extracted.intended_audience: UC Davis mathematics graduate students preparing a Master's thesis or Ph.D. dissertation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for UC Davis mathematics graduate students on preparing, formatting, and filing a Master's thesis or Ph.D. dissertation, including use of the department LaTeX template, filing procedures, accessibility requirements, and practical writing advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the LaTeX Dissertation Template (Dissertation Template 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: This template was originally created by Tyrell McAllister... In 2024, Greg DePaul updated the template to be Overleaf compatible. In 2026, Lisa Johnston reorganized and cleaned up the template to make it easier to edit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Download and use the department's 2026 template as a starting point. Note: This template is a good starting point but not an official Graduate Studies template — check current Graduate Studies filing and formatting requirements. Fill in Dissertation_Info.tex and maintain the file as you work. Older templates are archived for reference but may differ (e.g., page-numbering) or require extra work to stay current.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility requirement: WCAG 2.1 Level AA
rubrics_metrics.description: As of April 2026, all electronic dissertations and theses must meet the WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your electronic document complies with WCAG 2.1 Level AA prior to filing; consult Graduate Studies resources for specific accessibility steps and verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start early / keep notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Start early. Jot down notes when you talk to your advisor. Keep them somewhere that you'll be able to find them again. Often, you find that little notes you write can serve as a “seed” to start the writing process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture ideas and advisor comments promptly so they can be developed into drafts or sections later; early note-taking reduces last-minute scramble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write a little each day
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a little each day. Even just one hour a day, divided into four 15-minute sessions, goes a long way if you keep at it for a month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a consistent daily writing habit (short, regular sessions) to make steady progress rather than relying on sporadic marathon sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask for feedback early
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for feedback early. Get your advisor to look at small parts of drafts and chapters early on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek iterative feedback on small sections rather than waiting for full-chapter drafts; this helps catch problems early and keeps committee members engaged and aware of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep Dissertation_Info.tex and add citations as you go
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you pass your Qual, download the dissertation template! Fill in the Dissertation_Info.tex file, and add to your dissertation while you work on your research. After all, it's easier to write and cite as you go than to do it months/years later when that stuff isn't fresh in your mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate metadata and citation-related files incrementally to avoid large, error-prone backfills later; maintain bibliography and citation markup continuously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send draft to committee at least four weeks before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Grad Studies recommends sending your thesis or dissertation draft to your committee at least four weeks before the date you plan to file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although committees may need less time, check with committee members early and schedule to ensure availability; plan backwards from filing deadlines to allow review time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and uploading procedures (ProQuest ETD and GradSphere)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your committee members have signed your thesis or dissertation's title page, you will upload the completed document electronically to ProQuest ETD and upload the required paperwork through GradSphere. Grad Studies will review your dissertation to make sure that it is formatted correctly and let you know if any corrections need to be made. They will then inform you when your dissertation has been approved, after which time no further changes are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow current Graduate Studies instructions for ProQuest/GradSphere uploads. Expect a formatting review and possible corrections; do not plan to make substantive changes after Graduate Studies approval. Upload all required paperwork (signed title page, etc.) through GradSphere as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title page signature and upload requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page must be a single form signed by all committee members. Electronic signatures are accepted, and committee members may use any format or application to sign, except only typing their name. The title page in your ProQuest upload should be unsigned with blank signature lines. The signed title page is uploaded separately through GradSphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare two title-page versions: one unsigned for ProQuest (blank signature lines) and the separately uploaded signed single form for GradSphere. Ensure signatures meet the allowed formats (electronic signatures OK, but not mere typed names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule a pre-filing appointment if uncertain
rubrics_metrics.description: You can schedule a pre-filing appointment with a Senior Academic Advisor if you have questions or want to confirm that your materials are complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pre-filing appointment to verify that all paperwork, formatting, and file contents meet Graduate Studies and department expectations to avoid delays at final submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: This guide is unofficial — verify official Graduate Studies requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: This is an unofficial guide, and all information is subject to change. Current information about filing a thesis or dissertation at UC Davis can be found on the Graduate Studies page 'Filing Your Thesis Or Dissertation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the department page as advisory; always cross-check deadlines, formatting rules, and procedures with the official Graduate Studies website and current policy documents before final submission.
